title: Given coin denominations and a target amount, return the fewest number of coins needed to make that amount, or -1 if it cannot be made.
shortTitle: Coin Change — minimum coins to make an amount

s1_definition.profdef: Bottom-up DP where dp[a] is the minimum coins to make amount a, initialized to a sentinel (amount+1) and dp[0]=0. For each amount from 1 to target and each coin that fits, dp[a] = min(dp[a], dp[a−coin]+1). The answer is dp[target], or −1 if it remains the sentinel, computed in O(amount · coins) time.
s1_definition.analogy: A teller at National Bank of India must hand out an exact amount using the fewest notes from available denominations. For each amount, the best (fewest notes) is one more than the best for the amount left after removing one note, tried across every denomination that fits. You build the table upward to the target.
s1_definition.oneliner: dp[a] = min over coins of dp[a−coin] + 1; sentinel means unreachable, so return -1.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** Bottom-up DP where dp[a] is the minimum coins to make amount a, initialized to a sentinel (amount+1) and dp[0]=0. For each amount from 1 to target and each coin that fits, dp[a] = min(dp[a], dp[a−coin]+1). The answer is dp[target], or −1 if it remains the sentinel, computed in O(amount · coins) time.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** A teller at National Bank of India must hand out an exact amount using the fewest notes from available denominations. For each amount, the best (fewest notes) is one more than the best for the amount left after removing one note, tried across every denomination that fits. You build the table upward to the target.

**One line to remember:** dp[a] = min over coins of dp[a−coin] + 1; sentinel means unreachable, so return -1.

sections.s2_technical:
Create dp of size amount+1, fill with a sentinel larger than any real answer, and set dp[0] to zero because zero amount needs zero coins. For each amount a, try every coin that does not exceed a and relax the minimum. For example: `if (coin <= a) dp[a] = Math.min(dp[a], dp[a - coin] + 1);`.

Iterating amounts outward guarantees dp[a−coin] is already final when used, which is why this is unbounded (coins reusable): the inner coin loop may use the same denomination repeatedly across increasing amounts. At the end, if dp[target] is still the sentinel the target is unreachable, so return −1.

The time is O(amount · number of coins) and the space is O(amount). A senior nuance is that this is the minimization variant of the unbounded knapsack, and greedy (always take the largest coin) fails for arbitrary denominations, which is exactly why DP is required rather than greedy.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — At National Bank of India, an ATM must dispense an exact amount using the fewest notes from its available denominations, and some amounts cannot be dispensed at all. This is exactly how Coin Change works.

Problem 2 — A greedy largest-note-first approach can fail for certain denomination sets, so the minimum must be computed properly. This is exactly why bottom-up DP relaxes every coin for every amount.

The mini-project builds a `NoteDispenser`, a `BankLogFormatter`, and a runnable demo.

sections.s5_journey:
The input denominations are one, two, five with target eleven.

Step 1: dp[0] is zero and all other entries start at the sentinel twelve.

Step 2: Small amounts fill in: dp[1] is one, dp[2] is one (a single two), dp[5] is one (a single five).

Step 3: dp[11] relaxes across coins, finding five plus dp[6], where dp[6] is two (five plus one), giving three notes total.

Step 4: For target three with only a two-rupee note, dp[3] never improves past the sentinel, so the answer is minus one.

Step 5: The results are three notes for eleven and unreachable for three with only twos.

```text
2026-10-27T01:10:00Z [INFO] National Bank of India — ATM Note Dispenser (Coin Change)
2026-10-27T01:10:00Z [INFO] Amount 11 needs minimum 3 notes
2026-10-27T01:10:00Z [INFO] 11 → 3
2026-10-27T01:10:00Z [WARNING] Amount 3 cannot be dispensed
2026-10-27T01:10:00Z [INFO] 3 with {2} → -1
```
sections.s5b_flow:
```text
  dp[0]=0, dp[1..amount]=sentinel
    for a=1..11: dp[a]=min(dp[a], dp[a-coin]+1) over coins {1,2,5}
      dp[11] = 1 + dp[6] = 1 + 2 = 3
  unreachable (e.g. 3 with {2}) → dp stays sentinel → -1
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
Coin Change for the minimum number of coins is a bottom-up dynamic programming problem. I define dp of a as the fewest coins to make amount a, initialize every entry to a sentinel larger than any possible answer, and set dp of zero to zero because no coins are needed for a zero amount. Then for each amount from one up to the target I try every coin that fits and relax the value to the minimum of its current value and one plus dp of the amount remaining after that coin.

Iterating the amounts outward guarantees that the subproblem dp of amount-minus-coin is already final when I use it, and because the inner loop can pick the same denomination at every larger amount, coins are effectively unlimited. If dp of the target is still the sentinel at the end, the amount is unreachable and I return minus one.

In my project at National Bank of India, an ATM had to dispense an exact amount using the fewest notes from its available denominations, and some amounts were impossible with the loaded cassettes. I used this DP rather than a greedy largest-note-first rule, because greedy fails for arbitrary denomination sets, whereas the bottom-up relaxation always finds the true minimum or correctly reports that the amount cannot be dispensed.
